tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

# site.yml -- provisions the public web tier
#
# Originally written by mkovacs in 2019, Ubuntu 20.04 support added by Priya,
# then ported to 22.04 by whoever drew the short straw in 2023.
#
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod site.yml --limit web --diff
#
# NOTE: do not reorder the plays, the db play relies on facts gathered here.

- name: Common baseline for every host
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  gather_facts: True    # needed for ansible_distribution_release below

  vars:
    # proxy settings -- leave these empty outside the office network
    http_proxy: ~
    https_proxy: null
    no_proxy:
    ntp_servers: [0.de.pool.ntp.org, 1.de.pool.ntp.org,
                  2.de.pool.ntp.org,  # added after the March outage
                  time.cloudflare.com]
    base_packages:
      - curl
      - vim-nox
      - htop          # someone always asks for this
      - unattended-upgrades
      - python3-apt
    sysctl_settings: {"net.core.somaxconn": 4096, "vm.swappiness": 10,
                      "fs.file-max": 2_097_152}
    login_umask: "027"
    retry_policy: &retry
      retries: 5
      delay: 10
    # printed in /etc/motd, see the motd task below
    contacts:
      On call: ops-oncall@example.com
      Escalation lead: "Dana Whitfield <dana@example.com>"
      'Office hours': Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 CET

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh the apt cache if it is older than an hour
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        update_cache: true
        cache_valid_time: 3600

  tasks:
    - name: Install base packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: "{{ base_packages }}"
        state: present
        install_recommends: no
# sysctl values are also documented on the wiki, keep both in sync
    - name: Apply sysctl settings
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_set: yes
        reload: yes
      loop: "{{ sysctl_settings | dict2items }}"
          # the label keeps the output readable
      loop_control: {label: "{{ item.key }}"}

    - name: Set the default umask for login shells
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: /etc/login.defs
        regexp: '^UMASK\s+'
        line: "UMASK\t\t{{ login_umask }}"
        backup: yes

    # The banner needs the |2 indicator because its first line is indented
    # further than the rest; without it YAML guesses the indentation wrong.
    - name: Install the SSH login banner
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/issue.net
        content: |2
            ******************************************
            *  Authorized access only.               *
            ******************************************
          All connections are logged. Disconnect now if you are not an
          authorized user of Example Corp systems.
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'

    - name: Write the message of the day
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/motd
        content: >+
          This host is managed by Ansible. Manual changes will be
          overwritten on the next run, which usually happens within
          thirty minutes.

          On call: {{ contacts['On call'] }}


        mode: 0o644

    - name: Configure NTP servers
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/timesyncd.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf
        mode: "0644"
      notify: restart timesyncd

  handlers:
    - name: restart timesyncd
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: systemd-timesyncd
        state: restarted
        enabled: on


- name: Web servers
  hosts: web
  become: true
  serial: "25%"          # roll through the fleet a quarter at a time
  max_fail_percentage: 0
  vars:
    nginx_worker_connections: 1_024
    allowed_ports: &web_ports [80, 443]
    node_exporter_version: 1.8.2
    # TODO(priya): move these to group_vars once the staging inventory is gone
    upstreams:
      - {name: app_v1, host: 10.20.0.11, port: 8080, weight: 3}
      - {name: app_v2, host: 10.20.0.12, port: 8080, weight: 1, backup: yes}
    nginx_extra_headers:
      "X-Frame-Options": DENY
      "Strict-Transport-Security": "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
      Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

  roles:
    - role: geerlingguy.nginx
      vars:
        nginx_remove_default_vhost: true
    - { role: certbot, certbot_auto_renew: yes, certbot_auto_renew_hour: "3" }

  tasks:
    - name: Open the web ports in ufw
      community.general.ufw:
        rule: allow
        port: "{{ item }}"
        proto: tcp
      loop: *web_ports

    - name: Turn on ufw logging
      community.general.ufw:
        logging: 'on'

    - name: Download node exporter
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/releases/download/v{{ node_exporter_version }}/node_exporter-{{ node_exporter_version }}.linux-amd64.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/node_exporter.tar.gz
        checksum: "sha256:https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/releases/download/v{{ node_exporter_version }}/sha256sums.txt"
      register: download
      until: download is succeeded
      <<: *retry

    - name: Check that the nginx config is sane
      ansible.builtin.shell: |-
        set -o pipefail
        nginx -t 2>&1 | tee /var/log/nginx/last-config-test.log
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: false

    - name: Smoke test the health endpoint
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "https://{{ inventory_hostname }}/healthz"
        method: GET
        headers:
          "Accept": application/json
          "X-Request-Id": "ansible-{{ ansible_date_time.epoch }}"
          User-Agent: 'ansible-smoke-test/1.0 (+https://wiki.example.com/ops/web)'
        status_code: [200,
                      204]
        validate_certs: off    # staging still uses the self-signed cert
        return_content: no
      delegate_to: localhost
      <<: *retry
      tags: [smoke,
             never]

    - name: Remind the operator to update the change log
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: Deployment finished. Please record the change in the ops
          change log before closing the ticket, and mention any hosts
          that were skipped
      run_once: true


- name: Database replicas (the primary is still managed by hand)
  hosts: db_replicas
  become: yes
  gather_facts: no
  vars:
    pg_version: 15
    pg_settings:
      max_connections: 200
      shared_buffers: 4GB
      "effective_cache_size": 12GB
      random_page_cost: 1.1
      statement_timeout: 0        # disabled on replicas, reports run long
      log_min_duration_statement: 1_000
  tasks:
    - name: Render the postgresql.conf overrides
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/postgresql.auto.conf.j2
        dest: "/etc/postgresql/{{ pg_version }}/main/conf.d/90-ansible.conf"
        owner: postgres
        group: postgres
        mode: "0640"
      notify: reload postgres
  handlers:
    - name: reload postgres
      ansible.builtin.service: {name: "postgresql@{{ pg_version }}-main",
                                state: reloaded}

info:
  title: Invoicing API
  version: "2.14.0"
  description: |
    The Invoicing API lets partners create invoices, credit notes and payment
    reminders on behalf of their customers.

    ## Authentication

    All requests need a bearer token from the `/oauth/token` endpoint. Tokens
    expire after **15 minutes**; refresh them early rather than waiting for a `401`.

    ## Rate limits

    | Plan       | Requests / minute | Burst |
    |------------|------------------:|------:|
    | Starter    |               120 |    20 |
    | Business   |             1 200 |   100 |
    | Enterprise |         unlimited |   n/a |

    Questions? Write to <api-support@example.com>.
  contact:
    name: API support
    email: api-support@example.com
  license: {name: Proprietary, url: "https://example.com/legal/api-terms"}
  x-logo:
    url: https://developer.example.com/static/logo.svg
    altText: Example Invoicing
servers:
  - url: https://api.example.com/v2
    description: Production
  - url: https://sandbox.api.example.com/v2
    description: "Sandbox (data is wiped every Sunday at 02:00 UTC)"
  - url: "{scheme}://localhost:{port}/v2"
    description: Local development
    variables:
      scheme: {enum: [http, https], default: http}
      port: {default: "8080"}
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
tags:
  - name: Invoices
  - name: Credit notes
    description: Corrections to invoices that were already sent.
  - name: Admin
    description: >-
      Internal endpoints. They are not part of the public contract and may
      change without notice.
    x-internal: yes

paths:
  /invoices:
    get:
      tags: [Invoices]
      summary: List invoices
      operationId: listInvoices
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PageSize'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Cursor"
        - name: status
          in: query
          explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
              enum: [draft, sent, paid, overdue, void]
        - {name: customer_id, in: query, schema: {type: string, format: uuid}}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of invoices.
          headers:
            X-RateLimit-Remaining: &rate_limit_header
              description: Requests left in the current window.
              schema: {type: integer}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [data, next_cursor]
                properties:
                  data:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Invoice'}
                  next_cursor:
                    type: string
                    nullable: true
                    example: ~
        "401": &unauthorized
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        default: &problem
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'
    post:
      tags: [Invoices]
      summary: Create an invoice
      operationId: createInvoice
      parameters:
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: true
          description: A unique key per logical request. Retries with the same key return the original response instead of creating a second invoice.
          schema: {type: string, maxLength: 64}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/InvoiceInput'
            examples:
              minimal invoice:
                summary: Only the required fields
                value:
                  customer_id: 6f1c2b8e-3f5d-4c8e-9a51-0d2b7c1e4f90
                  currency: EUR
                  lines:
                    - {description: Consulting (March), quantity: 12, unit_price: "95.00"}
              "with discount and note":
                value:
                  customer_id: 6f1c2b8e-3f5d-4c8e-9a51-0d2b7c1e4f90
                  currency: CHF
                  note: "Merci pour votre confiance !"
                  discount_percent: 5
                  lines:
                    - description: Annual licence
                      quantity: 1
                      unit_price: "1490.00"
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created.
          headers:
            Location:
              schema: {type: string, format: uri}
            X-RateLimit-Remaining: *rate_limit_header
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Invoice'}
        "401": *unauthorized
        '409':
          description: An invoice with this `Idempotency-Key` already exists, but the request body is different.
        default: *problem

  /invoices/{invoice_id}:
    parameters:
      - name: invoice_id
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^INV-\\d{6}$"
    get:
      tags: [Invoices]
      operationId: getInvoice
      summary: Fetch a single invoice
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The invoice, as JSON or as the rendered PDF.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Invoice'}
            application/pdf:
              schema: {type: string, format: binary}
        '404': {description: No invoice with this number.}
        default: *problem
    delete:
      tags: [Invoices]
      operationId: voidInvoice
      summary: Void a draft invoice
      deprecated: True    # use POST /invoices/{invoice_id}/void instead; removed in v3
      responses:
        "204": {description: Voided.}
        default: *problem

  /admin/reindex:
    post:
      tags: [Admin]
      operationId: reindexSearch
      summary: Rebuild the invoice search index
      x-rate-limit-per-minute: .inf    # internal callers are not throttled
      x-codegen-ignore: on
      responses:
        "202":
          description: >+
            Accepted. The reindex runs in the background and usually
            finishes within a few minutes.

        default: *problem

components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
  parameters:
    PageSize:
      name: page_size
      in: query
      schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 200, default: 50}
    Cursor:
      name: cursor
      in: query
      description: Opaque cursor from `next_cursor` of the previous page. Do not try to parse it; the format has changed twice already.
      schema:
        type: string
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: The bearer token is missing, expired or revoked.
    Problem:
      description: An error in [RFC 7807](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807) format.
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    Money: &money
      type: string
      pattern: '^-?\d+\.\d{2}$'
      example: "149.90"
    InvoiceLine:
      type: object
      required: [description, quantity, unit_price]
      properties:
        description: {type: string, maxLength: 300}
        quantity:
          type: number
          minimum: 0
          exclusiveMinimum: true
        unit_price: *money
        vat_rate:
          type: number
          enum: [0, 2.6, 3.8, 7, 8.1, 19, 20]
          default: null    # null means "use the customer's default rate"
    InvoiceInput:
      type: object
      required: [customer_id, currency,
                 lines]
      properties:
        customer_id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        currency: {type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$', example: EUR}
        note:
          type: string
          nullable: yes
          maxLength: 2000
        discount_percent: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
        lines:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/InvoiceLine'
    Invoice:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/InvoiceInput'
        - type: object
          required: [number, status, total]
          properties:
            number: {type: string, example: INV-004217}
            status:
              type: string
              enum: [draft, sent, paid, overdue, void]
            total:
              <<: *money
              description: Sum of all lines after the discount, including VAT.
            sent_at: {type: string, format: date-time, nullable: true}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank"}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer, example: 422}
        detail: {type: string}

Changelog
=========

All notable changes to **tidyfmt** are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog][kac], and this project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning][semver] (mostly -- see the note under 2.0.0).  
Dates are ISO 8601, because we argued about it for three weeks in 2021.

<!-- Maintainers: add new entries under "Unreleased" and never edit released
     sections, except to fix broken links. The release script moves things. -->

## [Unreleased] ##

### Added

- `--check` now prints a unified diff when combined with `--diff`.

- Support for Quarto callout divs (`::: {.callout-note}`); thanks to
  Sofia R. for the initial patch ([#612]).

### Fixed

- Front matter that ends with `...` instead of `---` is no longer swallowed
  into the first paragraph.

- Tables with escaped pipes (`\|`) inside inline code keep their column count.

## [2.3.0] - 2026-09-30 ##

### Added
+ R Markdown: sentence wrapping when `wrap: sentence` is set under
  `editor_options` in the front matter.
+ New option `--line-width` (default: 80). Alias: `-w`.
+ The configuration can now live in `pyproject.toml`:

  ```toml
  [tool.tidyfmt]
  line-width = 100
  wrap = "sentence"
  ```

### Changed 
+ The minimum supported Python version is now 3.9.
+ The default for `--end-of-line` changed from `lf` to `auto`. If you relied on the old behaviour, set it explicitly in your configuration file or pass `--end-of-line=lf` on the command line.

### Deprecated
+ `--no-wrap` is deprecated in favour of `--wrap=preserve` and will be removed in 3.0.

## [2.2.1] — 2026-05-14

### Fixed

1) Crash on empty YAML documents between two `---` markers ([#580]).
2) Windows: files with CRLF line endings were rewritten with mixed endings
   when a block scalar was the last thing in the file.
3) Pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> once now stops `--watch` mode; before,
   it needed two presses on some terminals.

## [2.2.0] - 2026-03-02

### Added

* Experimental support for Python files: Markdown in comment blocks and string
  assignments marked with `# fmt: markdown` is formatted.

  This is opt-in for now. Enable it with:

      tidyfmt --experimental python src/

* Footnotes are supported[^1].

### Changed

* Headings are normalised to ATX style. Setext headings in existing files are
  kept unless you pass `--normalize-headings`.
* Formatting the CPython docs went from 41 s to 6.8 s on an M2 laptop, mostly
  thanks to a smarter 2<sup>nd</sup> pass over inline content.

### Fixed

* An emoji at the end of a wrapped line no longer counts as two columns 🎉 (#541)
* Non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) are kept as they are.   

***

## 2.1.0 - 2025-11-20 ##

A small release, mostly bug fixes. Upgrading is recommended for everyone on 2.0.x.

- **YAML:** comments between sequence items are no longer moved to the end of
  the previous item.
- **YAML:** block scalars with an explicit indentation indicator (`|2`) keep
  their indicator.  
  Previously the indicator was dropped, which changed the meaning of the
  document when the first line started with spaces.
- **Markdown:** reference definitions with titles in parentheses, like
  `[x]: https://example.com (Example)`, stay on one line.
- Typo fixes in the docs by Zoë Lindqvist, Mateus Araújo and 田中さくら. Thank you!

2.0.0 – 2025-06-01
------------------

This is a big one. Please read the [migration guide][migrate] before upgrading.\
It also lists the deprecation warnings you should fix first.

### Breaking changes

1. The configuration file was renamed from `.tidyfmtrc` to `tidyfmt.toml`.
   The old name is still read, with a warning.
2. Exit codes changed:

   | Code | Meaning                         |
   |:----:|:--------------------------------|
   | 0    | nothing to do                   |
   | 1    | files would be reformatted      |
   | 2    | invalid input (parse error)     |
   | 3    | internal error \| please report |

3. The Python API moved from `tidyfmt.api` to `tidyfmt`. The old imports keep
   working until 3.0.

### Removed

- Support for Python 3.7.
- The `--legacy-tables` option. It hasn't really worked since 1.4 anyway.

___

## 1.x

The 1.x series is no longer maintained. Its changelog is kept in
[docs/history/CHANGELOG-1.x.md](docs/history/CHANGELOG-1.x.md) and on the old
website, <https://tidyfmt.example.org/history/1.x/changelog.html#release-1-9-3-2024-12-02-security-fixes-and-the-final-release-of-the-1-x-line>.

> **Note**  
> If you are still on 1.x, the last release (1.9.3) contains a security fix
> for the YAML loader. Upgrade at least to that:
>
> ```sh
> pip install "tidyfmt>=1.9.3,<2"
> ```

[^1]: Using the `[^label]` syntax from PHP Markdown Extra and GitHub. Footnote

Contributing to Kestrel ======================= First off: thank you for taking the time to contribute! ❤️ Kestrel is maintained by volunteers in their spare time, so please be patient while waiting for a review. [![Build status][ci-badge]][ci] [![Chat on Matrix][matrix-badge]][matrix] Table of contents ----------------- 1. [Code of conduct](#code-of-conduct) 2. [Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs) 3. [Setting up a development environment](#setting-up-a-development-environment) 4. [Pull requests](#pull-requests) 5. [Style guide](#style-guide) ## Code of conduct ## This project follows the [Contributor Covenant][coc]. By participating you are expected to uphold it. Please report unacceptable behaviour to . ## Reporting bugs ## Before opening an issue, please: * search the [existing issues][issues], including the closed ones; * check that you are on the latest release (`kestrel --version`); * try to reduce the problem to a minimal example. A config file with 20 lines is much easier to debug than one with 2,000. If the bug only happens with a large input, attach the file to the issue instead of pasting it inline. When you file the issue, include - what you did, - what you expected to happen, and - what actually happened (the full error output, not a screenshot of it). ## Setting up a development environment You need Python 3.10 or newer and [`uv`][uv]. Then: ~~~bash git clone https://github.com/kestrel-dev/kestrel.git cd kestrel uv sync --all-extras uv run pre-commit install ~~~ Run the tests with `uv run pytest`. A few of them need network access; skip those with uv run pytest -m "not network"
Notes for Windows users Use PowerShell, not `cmd.exe`. If `uv` is not found after installing it, open a new terminal window: the installer updates `PATH`, but shells that are already running don't see the change.
Long paths must be enabled (`git config --system core.longpaths true`), otherwise the test fixtures can't be checked out.
## Pull requests + Small, focused pull requests get reviewed much faster than large ones. + Every pull request needs a changelog entry, unless it only touches tests or docs. + The steps, roughly: 1. Fork the repository and create a branch from `main`. 2. Make your change, and add tests for it. 3. Run the full check suite: uv run nox This runs the linters, the type checker and the tests on every supported Python version, so it takes a while. Go and make a coffee ☕. 4. Push your branch and open a pull request. Please fill in the template. + A maintainer will review your pull request. You may be asked to make changes; that's normal and not a judgement of your work. 🙂 ### Commit messages We loosely follow [Conventional Commits][cc]. The first line should be at most 72 characters, the body can be as long as needed.\ Some good first lines: fix(yaml): keep comments between sequence items feat(cli): add the --line-width option docs: explain the release process > **Tip:** if you get this wrong, don't worry -- we squash-merge most pull > requests and can fix the message then. What *does* matter: > > - one logical change per commit, if you don't want us to squash; > - no merge commits from `main` into your branch. Rebase instead: > > ```console > $ git fetch upstream > $ git rebase upstream/main > ``` ## Style guide | What | Tool | Configured in | |:------------------|:-----------------:|-------------------:| | Formatting | `ruff format` | `pyproject.toml` | | Linting | `ruff check` | `pyproject.toml` | | Type checking | mypy (strict) | `mypy.ini` | | Shell scripts | shellcheck | `.shellcheckrc` | | Commit hooks | pre-commit | `.pre-commit-config.yaml` | | Regex alternation | escape `\|` in tables | n/a | A few conventions that the tools don't check: 1) Write docstrings in the Google style. 2) Public functions need type hints. Private helpers *should* have them. 3) Prefer `pathlib.Path` over `os.path`.[why?](https://treyhunner.com/2018/12/why-you-should-be-using-pathlib/) ### Documentation The docs live in `docs/` and are built with MkDocs. To preview them, type uv run mkdocs serve and open . Screenshots go into `docs/img/` and should look roughly like this one: ![Screenshot of the kestrel TUI][screenshot] Translations are welcome (there are partial 日本語 and Français versions), but please coordinate in the [discussion forum][forum] first, so that two people don't translate the same page.[^translations] ## Releasing (maintainers only) # 1. Update `CHANGELOG.md` and bump the version in `pyproject.toml`. 2. Tag the release: `git tag -s v1.2.3 -m "v1.2.3"`. 3. Push the tag. CI builds and uploads the wheels; check afterwards. *** Thanks again! If anything in this document is unclear, that's a bug -- please [open an issue][issues] about it. [^translations]: Translations that fall more than two minor versions behind are hidden from the navigation until someone updates them. fjord — semantic diffs for YAML, TOML and JSON

# fjord `fjord` compares configuration files by **meaning**, not by text. Reordered keys, different quoting styles or a change of indentation don't show up as differences; a value that went from `"8080"` to `8080` does. ```console $ fjord diff old/values.yaml new/values.yaml ~ spec.replicas: 3 → 5 + spec.template.metadata.annotations["prometheus.io/scrape"]: "true" - spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[2] (HTTP_PROXY) ``` > ⚠️ fjord is still below 1.0. The command line is stable, the library API is not. ## Features ## - Understands YAML 1.1 *and* 1.2 (yes, `on: yes` is handled correctly) - Multi-document YAML streams, anchors, aliases and merge keys - TOML 1.0, JSON and JSON5 - Output as text, JSON or a GitHub-flavoured Markdown table - Fast: diffs a 40 MB Helm render in well under a second[^bench] ## Installation Pick whatever suits you: + **Cargo** ```sh cargo install fjord --locked ``` + **Homebrew** (macOS and Linux) brew install fjord-tools/tap/fjord + **Pre-built binaries** for Linux, macOS and Windows are attached to every [release][releases]. Please verify them against the published SHA-256 checksums. + **From source:** see [`docs/building.md`](docs/building.md). ## Usage fjord diff [OPTIONS] fjord explain The options you will probably need: | Option | Short | Default | Description | |-------------------|:-----:|:-------:|-----------------------------------------------------| | `--format ` | `-f` | `text` | `text`, `json` or `markdown` | | `--ignore ` | `-i` | | Ignore a path, e.g. `metadata.labels`; repeatable | | `--yaml-version` | | `auto` | `1.1`, `1.2` or `auto` | | `--color ` | | `auto` | `always` \| `never` \| `auto` | | `--exit-code` | `-e` | off | Exit with status 1 if there are differences | In the interactive pager, press q to quit and / to search. ### Ignoring paths 1) Use `--ignore` on the command line for one-off runs. 2) For anything permanent, list the paths in a `.fjordignore` file: ~~~gitignore # generated by Helm, changes on every render metadata.annotations["helm.sh/chart"] metadata.labels.chart ~~~ 3) Paths support `*` (exactly one segment) and `**` (any number of segments). ### Using it in CI > fjord exits with status 0 when the files are equivalent and 1 when they differ > (with `--exit-code`). A typical GitLab CI job: > > ```yaml > config-drift: > script: > - fjord diff --exit-code deployed.yaml rendered.yaml > ``` > > Add `--format markdown` to post the result as a merge request comment. ## FAQ **Why not just `diff <(yq -P a.yaml) <(yq -P b.yaml)`?** That works for simple cases, but `yq` doesn't know that `0o14` and `12` are the same number in YAML 1.2, or that a merge key expands to the same mapping as the long form. **Does it work on Windows?**\ Yes. Paths with backslashes work, and CRLF files are compared without complaint. **Is the name an acronym?** No, it's just a nice word: Norwegian *fjord*, from Old Norse *fjǫrðr*. *** ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are very welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; for bigger changes, open an issue to discuss the design before writing code. Thanks to everyone who has contributed so far, especially the people who translated the documentation into Deutsch, Español and 简体中文. 🙏 ## License Licensed under either of * Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or ) * MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or ) at your option. [^bench]: Measured on a 2023 laptop with `hyperfine`; see [the benchmark notes][bench] for the exact setup. Your mileage will vary. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synchronise the translation catalogues with the English source strings.

Run it from the repository root::

    python tools/sync_translations.py --check

Originally written for the 2.x branch; the catalogue handling was rewritten in
2023 when we moved from gettext PO files to JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import dataclasses
import datetime
import json
import re
import string
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

LOCALES_DIR = Path("locales")
SOURCE_LOCALE = "en"
PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"\{[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\}|%\([a-z_]+\)[sd]")
OBSOLETE_PREFIX = '#~ '

# fmt: markdown
USAGE = """
# sync_translations

Keeps every catalogue in `locales/` in step with the English source strings. It *never* deletes a translation on its own: obsolete entries are prefixed with `#~` so that a human can decide what to do with them.

Typical workflow:

1. Change or add strings in `locales/en/messages.json`.
2. Run `python tools/sync_translations.py --fix` to add the new keys to every other locale.
3. Commit, then ask the translators in the `#i18n` channel to fill in the gaps.

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | everything is in sync |
| 1 | missing or obsolete keys were found (only with `--check`) |
| 2 | a catalogue could not be read or parsed |

**Note:** `--check` is what CI runs. Use `--fix` locally, but *never* in CI, because it rewrites the files in place.
"""

# fmt: markdown
# How placeholders are compared
# =============================
#
# A translation is only accepted if it uses *exactly* the same placeholders as the English source string, in any order. Both the `str.format` style (`{name}`) and the old printf style (`%(name)s`) are recognised, but mixing the two in one string is reported as an error.
#
# - Placeholders are compared as multisets, so `{n} of {n}` needs two `{n}` in the translation as well.
# - Plural forms are checked one by one; a locale with three plural forms (Polish, Russian, ...) needs all three.
# - HTML tags are **not** checked. That would be nice, but the false positive rate was terrible when we tried it in 2022.


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Problem:
    locale: str
    key: str
    kind: str  # "missing", "obsolete" or "placeholders"
    detail: str = ""

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        suffix = f" ({self.detail})" if self.detail else ""
        return f"{self.locale}: {self.key}: {self.kind}{suffix}"


def load_catalogue(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Load a JSON catalogue and flatten nested objects into dotted keys."""
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        data = json.load(fh)

    flat: dict[str, str] = {}

    def walk(prefix: str, node: object) -> None:
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            for key, value in node.items():
                walk(f"{prefix}.{key}" if prefix else key, value)
        elif isinstance(node, str):
            flat[prefix] = node
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"{path}: {prefix}: expected a string, got {type(node).__name__}")

    walk("", data)
    return flat


def placeholders(text: str) -> Counter[str]:
    return Counter(PLACEHOLDER_RE.findall(text))


def compare(source: dict[str, str], target: dict[str, str], locale: str) -> list[Problem]:
    problems = []
    for key, english in source.items():
        translated = target.get(key)
        if translated is None:
            problems.append(Problem(locale, key, "missing"))
        elif translated == "" or translated.startswith(OBSOLETE_PREFIX):
            continue  # not translated yet, or parked on purpose
        elif placeholders(english) != placeholders(translated):
            expected = ", ".join(sorted(placeholders(english))) or "none"
            problems.append(Problem(locale, key, "placeholders", f"expected {expected}"))
    for key in sorted(target.keys() - source.keys()):
        if not target[key].startswith(OBSOLETE_PREFIX):
            problems.append(Problem(locale, key, 'obsolete'))
    return problems


# fmt: markdown
REPORT_TEMPLATE = r"""
## Translation report, $date

The catalogues were read from `$locales_dir`. On the Windows build agents that is something like `C:\agent\_work\1\s\locales`, which is why the paths below may contain backslashes.

* **$n_missing** missing keys
* **$n_obsolete** obsolete keys
* **$n_placeholders** placeholder mismatches

Placeholders are found with the regular expression `\{[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\}|%\([a-z_]+\)[sd]`. A translator who needs a literal brace can write `{{` or `}}`, exactly as in the English strings.
"""


def write_report(problems: list[Problem], out: Path) -> None:
    counts = Counter(p.kind for p in problems)
    text = string.Template(REPORT_TEMPLATE).safe_substitute(
        date=datetime.date.today().isoformat(),
        locales_dir=LOCALES_DIR,
        n_missing=counts["missing"],
        n_obsolete=counts["obsolete"],
        n_placeholders=counts["placeholders"],
    )
    lines = [text.strip(), ""]
    for problem in sorted(problems, key=lambda p: (p.locale, p.key)):
        lines.append(f"- `{problem.locale}` / `{problem.key}`: {problem.kind} {problem.detail}".rstrip())
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def fix_catalogue(path: Path, target: dict[str, str], problems: list[Problem]) -> None:
    for problem in problems:
        if problem.kind == "missing":
            target[problem.key] = ""
        elif problem.kind == "obsolete":
            target[problem.key] = OBSOLETE_PREFIX + target[problem.key]
    # NOTE: this writes the flattened form; load_catalogue() reads both.
    # TODO: keep the key order of the existing file (see #233)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(target, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Synchronise translation catalogues.",
        epilog="Run with --usage for the full documentation.",
    )
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument('--check', action='store_true', help='only report problems (the default)')
    mode.add_argument('--fix', action='store_true', help='add missing keys and park obsolete ones')
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, metavar="FILE", help="also write a Markdown report to FILE")
    parser.add_argument("--usage", action="store_true", help="print the long help text and exit")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.usage:
        print(USAGE.strip())
        return 0

    try:
        source = load_catalogue(LOCALES_DIR / SOURCE_LOCALE / "messages.json")
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot read the source catalogue: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    problems: list[Problem] = []
    for locale_dir in sorted(p for p in LOCALES_DIR.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        if locale_dir.name == SOURCE_LOCALE:
            continue
        path = locale_dir / "messages.json"
        try:
            target = load_catalogue(path)
        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
            print(f"error: {path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        found = compare(source, target, locale_dir.name)
        if args.fix and found:
            fix_catalogue(path, target, found)
        problems.extend(found)

    for problem in problems:
        print(problem)
    if args.report:
        write_report(problems, args.report)
    #print(f"{len(problems)} problem(s)")  # handy when debugging
    return 1 if problems and not args.fix else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# bikeshare_summary.R
#
# Cleans the monthly trip exports from the bike-share operator and writes the
# summary tables used in the quarterly mobility report.
#
# Authors: J. Okafor (2021), M. Lindgren (2022-), with fixes from the GIS team
# Usage:   Rscript R/bikeshare_summary.R data/raw/2026-09
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
})

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
raw_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else file.path("data", "raw", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m"))
out_dir = file.path("output", basename(raw_dir))
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Trips shorter than this are almost always docking problems (people re-docking
# a bike that did not lock properly), so they are dropped.
min_duration_sec <- 90
max_duration_sec <- 6 * 60 * 60  # anything longer is a lost or stolen bike

# Swedish public holidays that fall on weekdays in 2026.
# TODO: use the timeDate package instead of maintaining this list by hand
holidays <- as_date(c("2026-01-01", "2026-01-06", "2026-04-03", "2026-04-06",
                      "2026-05-01", "2026-05-14", "2026-06-19", "2026-12-24",
                      "2026-12-25", "2026-12-31"))

# fmt: markdown
#' Read and clean one month of trip data
#'
#' The operator has changed the export format twice, so this function accepts all three variants and returns a tibble with consistent column names. Columns that only exist in the newer exports (like `rideable_type`) are filled with `NA` for older files.
#'
#' Cleaning steps, in this order:
#'
#' 1. drop trips with a missing start *or* end station,
#' 2. drop trips shorter than `min_duration_sec` or longer than `max_duration_sec`,
#' 3. convert the timestamps from UTC to **Europe/Stockholm** local time.
#'
#' | Export version | Used from | Start station column |
#' |----------------|-----------|----------------------|
#' | v1             | 2019-04   | `start_station`      |
#' | v2             | 2021-01   | `from_station_id`    |
#' | v3             | 2023-06   | `start_station_id`   |
#'
#' @param path Path to a CSV file, optionally gzipped.
#' @return A tibble with one row per trip.
read_trips <- function(path) {
  trips <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 10000)

  # rename the v1 and v2 columns to the v3 names
  if ("from_station_id" %in% names(trips)) {
    trips <- rename(trips, start_station_id = from_station_id, end_station_id = to_station_id)
  } else if ("start_station" %in% names(trips)) {
    trips <- rename(trips, start_station_id = start_station, end_station_id = end_station)
  }
  if (!"rideable_type" %in% names(trips)) {
    trips$rideable_type <- NA_character_
  }

  trips |>
    filter(!is.na(start_station_id), !is.na(end_station_id)) |>
    mutate(
      started_at = with_tz(ymd_hms(started_at, tz = "UTC"), "Europe/Stockholm"),
      ended_at = with_tz(ymd_hms(ended_at, tz = "UTC"), "Europe/Stockholm"),
      duration_sec = as.numeric(difftime(ended_at, started_at, units = "secs"))
    ) |>
    filter(between(duration_sec, min_duration_sec, max_duration_sec))
}

# fmt: markdown
report_intro <- "
## Bike-share trips, %s

This summary covers **%s trips** that passed the cleaning rules. Trips shorter than %d seconds or longer than six hours were removed, as were trips without a start or end station; see `read_trips()` for the details.

Things to keep in mind when reading the numbers:

- station IDs were renumbered in June 2023, so station-level comparisons across that date are *not* meaningful;
- e-bikes are only recorded separately from 2023 onwards;
- weekends and public holidays (*helgdagar*) are grouped together.
"

files <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = r"(\.csv(\.gz)?$)", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(files) == 0) {
  stop("No trip files found in ", raw_dir, call. = FALSE)
}
message("Reading ", length(files), " file(s) from ", raw_dir)

trips <- bind_rows(lapply(files, read_trips))

by_day <- trips %>%
  mutate(day = as_date(started_at),
         weekend = wday(day, week_start = 1) >= 6 | day %in% holidays) %>%
  group_by(day, weekend) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trips = n(),
    median_min = median(duration_sec) / 60,
    share_ebike = mean(rideable_type == "electric_bike", na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

top_stations <- trips |>
  count(start_station_id, name = "departures", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)

write_csv(by_day, file.path(out_dir, "trips_by_day.csv"))
write_csv(top_stations, file.path(out_dir, "top_stations.csv"), na = "")

# ---- plot -------------------------------------------------------------------

p <- ggplot(by_day, aes(x = day, y = n_trips, fill = weekend)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#4C78A8", `TRUE` = "#F58518"),
                    labels = c("Weekday", "Weekend / holiday"), name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Trips per day, %s", basename(raw_dir)),
    x = NULL, y = "Trips",
    caption = "Source: operator open data export, cleaned with bikeshare_summary.R"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "trips_per_day.png"), p, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)

intro <- sprintf(report_intro, basename(raw_dir), format(nrow(trips), big.mark = " "), min_duration_sec)
writeLines(intro, file.path(out_dir, "intro.md"))

message("Done. Output written to ", normalizePath(out_dir))

---
title: "Air quality in Lyon, 2019–2025"
subtitle: Exploratory analysis of the hourly NO₂ and PM₂.₅ measurements
author:
  - name: Camille Durand
    affiliation: Observatoire régional de l'air
    orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097
  - name: Tobias Reinholt
    affiliation: Université Lyon 1
date: 2026-10-12
date-modified: last-modified
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    code-fold: show
    number-sections: true
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrartcl
    papersize: a4
    keep-tex: false
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  cache: true
jupyter: python3
lang: en-GB
---

## Summary {.unnumbered}

Annual mean NO₂ concentrations at the urban background stations fell by about a third between 2019 and 2025. Most of that decrease happened in 2020 and has not reversed since, which matches what has been reported for other French cities [@lefevre2023; @eea2024, pp. 12–15]. PM₂.₅ shows a much weaker trend. The low-emission zone (ZFE) introduced in 2022 may have contributed, but our data alone cannot separate its effect from the general renewal of the vehicle fleet.

::: {.callout-note}
## About the data

All measurements come from the regional monitoring network and were downloaded on 2 October 2026. Values that the network operator flagged as invalid were removed before any analysis. Hourly values are in µg/m³, annual means are calendar-year means.
:::

## Data

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

STATIONS = ["Lyon Centre", "Gerland", "Croix-Rousse", "Villeurbanne"]
raw = pd.read_parquet("data/hourly_2019_2025.parquet")
raw = raw[raw["station"].isin(STATIONS)]
valid = raw[raw["flag"] == "valid"].copy()
valid["year"] = valid["timestamp"].dt.year
```

The cleaned data set contains `{python} f"{len(valid):,}"` hourly values from `{python} len(STATIONS)` stations. Coverage is above 90 % for every station and year except Gerland in 2021, when the NO₂ analyser was replaced (@tbl-coverage). We kept that year, but its annual mean should be read with care.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of valid hourly values per station and year (%)."
coverage = (
    raw.assign(year=raw["timestamp"].dt.year, ok=raw["flag"].eq("valid"))
    .pivot_table(index="station", columns="year", values="ok", aggfunc="mean")
    .mul(100)
    .round(1)
)
coverage
```

## Methods

For each station $s$ and year $y$ we compute the annual mean

$$
\bar{c}_{s,y} = \frac{1}{|H_{s,y}|} \sum_{h \in H_{s,y}} c_{s,h}
$$ {#eq-annual-mean}

where $H_{s,y}$ is the set of valid hours and $c_{s,h}$ the measured concentration. Trends are estimated with the Theil–Sen estimator on deseasonalised monthly means, which is robust against the occasional outlier month [@sen1968; @carslaw2012]. Confidence intervals come from 1 000 block-bootstrap resamples with a block length of 12 months. We did not adjust for meteorology^[A meteorological normalisation with boosted regression trees is planned for the next version of this report.], so year-to-year differences of a few µg/m³ should not be over-interpreted.

## Results

### Nitrogen dioxide

```{python}
#| label: fig-no2-trend
#| fig-cap: "Annual mean NO₂ by station. The dashed line marks the start of the ZFE in 2022."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
annual = valid.groupby(["station", "year"])["no2"].mean().unstack("station")
ax = annual.plot(marker="o")
ax.axvline(2022, linestyle="--", color="grey", linewidth=1)
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.set_ylabel("NO₂ (µg/m³)")
plt.tight_layout()
```

@fig-no2-trend shows the same pattern at every station: a sharp drop in 2020, a partial rebound in 2021 and a slow decline after that. Lyon Centre, the station closest to heavy traffic, still has the highest concentrations. Its annual mean was `{python} round(annual.loc[2025, "Lyon Centre"], 1)` µg/m³ in 2025, which is below the EU limit value of 40 µg/m³ but well above the WHO guideline of 10 µg/m³ [@who2021].

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
The Theil–Sen slopes are between −1.1 and −1.9 µg/m³ per year, and all of the 95 % intervals exclude zero. Gerland has the widest interval, which is not surprising given the gap in 2021. If we drop 2020 entirely, as a sensitivity check, the slopes shrink by roughly a quarter but remain negative.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
| Station      | Slope | 95 % CI        |
|:-------------|------:|:---------------|
| Lyon Centre  |  −1.9 | −2.6 to −1.2   |
| Gerland      |  −1.4 | −2.5 to −0.3   |
| Croix-Rousse |  −1.1 | −1.6 to −0.6   |
| Villeurbanne |  −1.3 | −1.9 to −0.8   |

: Trend in annual mean NO₂, µg/m³ per year {#tbl-slopes}
:::

::::

### Fine particles

PM₂.₅ is only measured at two of the four stations. The concentrations are lower and the year-to-year variation is dominated by a few episodes, most notably the Saharan dust events in spring 2022 and the wildfire smoke in August 2023. After removing those days the trend is slightly negative, but the interval includes zero (@tbl-slopes has the NO₂ numbers for comparison).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Known issue with the 2021 Gerland data

The replacement analyser at Gerland reported values about 8 % higher than the old one during the two-week overlap. We have not corrected for this. If you need a consistent series for Gerland, use 2022 onwards or apply the correction factor from the network's calibration report.
:::

## Conclusions

NO₂ has gone down, PM₂.₅ has hardly moved, and the ZFE effect cannot be identified from these data alone. A difference-in-differences design that compares stations inside and outside the zone would be the obvious next step; @eq-annual-mean defines the inputs such a comparison would use.

::: {.callout-tip}
To reproduce this report, run `quarto render report.qmd` from the project root. The first run takes about ten minutes because the parquet file has to be cached.
:::

## References {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

---
title: "Onboarding experiment: does the checklist improve week-4 retention?"
author: "Product Analytics — R. Haddad, L. Moreau"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
  word_document: default
bibliography: [references.bib, packages.bib]
link-citations: yes
params:
  experiment_id: "onb-2026-07"
  alpha: 0.05
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
```

```{r packages-bib}
#| include: false
knitr::write_bib(c("tidyverse", "broom", "knitr"), file = "packages.bib")
```

# Background

In July 2026 we replaced the five-screen onboarding tour with a short checklist that new users can work through at their own pace. The idea was simple. Users who create at least one project in their first session are much more likely to come back (approx. three times as likely in the 2025 cohorts), and the checklist makes that step more obvious than the tour did. Earlier experiments on the welcome e-mail moved week-4 retention by one to two percentage points [@haddad2025], so we did not expect anything dramatic.

This report analyses experiment `r params$experiment_id`.
It was pre-registered in the analytics wiki on 30 June 2026, and the analysis below follows that plan except where noted. Deviations are marked with a dagger (†).

# Data

```{r load}
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime("data/onboarding_users.csv")
users <- read_csv("data/onboarding_users.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = c("tour", "checklist")))
n_raw <- nrow(users)
users <- filter(users, !is_internal, !is_bot)
n_excluded <- n_raw - nrow(users)
```

The raw export contains `r format(n_raw, big.mark = ",")` accounts created between 7 July and 3 August 2026. We excluded `r n_excluded` accounts that belong to employees or were flagged as bots by the fraud team. Assignment was random at the account level with a 50/50 split, and a sample ratio mismatch test showed no problems ($p = 0.62$). Sign-up channels differ a lot (e.g. paid search vs. organic), but the randomisation balanced them well; the largest difference between the arms was 0.4 percentage points.

The outcome is *week-4 retention*: an account counts as retained if it was
active on at least one day between day 22 and day 28 after sign-up. This is the
same definition the growth team has used since 2024, so the numbers are
comparable with earlier experiments [see @kohavi2020, chap. 7, on why the metric must be fixed up front].

# Results

```{r retention-table}
#| tab.cap: "Week-4 retention by variant."
retention <- users |>
  group_by(variant) |>
  summarise(users = n(), retained = sum(active_week4), rate = mean(active_week4))
kable(retention, digits = 3, col.names = c("Variant", "Users", "Retained", "Rate"))
```

```{r test}
test <- prop.test(retention$retained, retention$users)
diff_pp <- 100 * diff(retention$rate)
ci_pp <- -100 * rev(test$conf.int)
```

Let $p_c$ and $p_t$ be the retention rates with the tour and with the checklist. We test $H_0\colon p_t = p_c$ against the two-sided alternative, using the usual normal approximation
$$
z = \frac{\hat p_t - \hat p_c}{\sqrt{\hat p\,(1 - \hat p)\left(\frac{1}{n_t} + \frac{1}{n_c}\right)}},
$$
where $\hat p$ is the pooled rate. The checklist group retained `r round(diff_pp, 1)` percentage points more users (95 % CI `r round(ci_pp[1], 1)` to `r round(ci_pp[2], 1)`). That is more than we expected. It is also close to the upper end of what the power analysis said we could plausibly see, which made us a little suspicious, so we looked at the result from a few other angles before writing it up.

```{r fig-retention}
#| fig.cap: "Share of users active on each day after sign-up. Shaded bands are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig.width: 7
#| fig.height: 4
#| out.width: "85%"
daily <- read_csv("data/onboarding_daily_activity.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ggplot(daily, aes(day, share_active, colour = variant, fill = variant)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Days since sign-up", y = "Active users", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The two curves separate on the first day and stay apart (Fig. 1). If this were a novelty effect, we would expect the gap to close after the first week; it does not. The gap is somewhat larger on mobile than on desktop, i.e. 2.9 vs. 1.8 points, but the interaction is not significant and the comparison was not pre-registered (†), so we do not want to read much into it.

We did not use CUPED or any other variance reduction [@deng2013]. Most accounts have no history before sign-up, so there is little to adjust for.

# Limitations

- The experiment ran during the summer holidays in most of Europe. New users in July and August are, on average, more often students and hobbyists than teams. They may respond differently to onboarding changes.
- Week-4 retention is a proxy. What we actually care about is whether these accounts convert to a paid plan, and we will not know that for another two months.
- We tested only one version of the checklist. The effect may depend heavily on the wording of the individual items.^[The copy was written in a single afternoon by Dr. Moreau and was never tested on its own.]

> **Decision needed by 1 December.** The product team wants to ship before the end-of-year freeze. If we wait for the conversion data, the change slips to January.

# Recommendation

Ship the checklist to all new users, keep a 5 % holdout for three months, and revisit the conversion numbers in the Q1 review. If the holdout confirms the effect, the next experiment should test a shorter checklist with three items instead of five.

# References
